sentences.text: Shri Himanshu Paliwal, learned counsel for the appellant  Shri Arun Gupta, learned counsel for the respondent [R-3  ORDER Heard on I.A. No.2094/2023, which is an application for condonation of delay.
There is a delay of 33 days in fling the present appeal.
For the reasons stated in the application, I.A. No.2094/2023 is allowed and disposed of.
The delay in filing the present appeal is condoned.
2. Also heard on I.A. No.6507/2025, an application for dispensing with the service of notice upon respondent Nos.1/driver & owner.
In view of the fact that only quantum of compensation has been challenged and liability of insurance company is not under dispute, I.A. No.6507/2025 is allowed.
The matter is being heard finally in absence of owner and driver.

3. The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 05.07.2022 passed in claim case No.138/2017 whereby challenging the quantum of compensation.
4. The liability of insurance company is not under dispute.

5. The short facts of case are that on 02.08.2016 at around 08.45 p.m. the appellant was walking towards tea-stall for taking tea, when he reached in front of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35780 2 MA-5449-2022 Standard Public School, Khandwa Road, the respondent No.2 came driving car number MP09-CQ-9582 in rash and negligent manner and dashed into the appellant because of which he sustained grievous injuries on his right lower limb, which got Dharasingh vs Manoj Rathore on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32127705/
1 fractured.
He was operated upon and implant of rod was inserted into his leg for the crush injuries suffered by him.
He also received injuries on other parts of his body.

6. The claimant/appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him, claims tribunal after recording evidence concluded that the accident occurred due to fault of the driver of the insured vehicle and consequently, a total compensation of Rs.3,41,470/- was awarded to the appellant.

The claims tribunal while awarding this compensation has held in para 14 that the appellant has suffered 15% permanent disability based on the statement of Dr. Ashish Mehrotra, AW-2.
7.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that this conclusion of the claims tribunal is not correct in view of the fact that the appellant was a driver and looking to the nature of his job, the loss of earning capacity is much more than 15% as he is not able to drive the vehicle after the accident and consequential permanent disability.

He further submits that in other heads meager amount has been awarded and total compensation of Rs.15000/- has been awarded for pain and suffering as well as loss of amenities of life and for special diet, attendants and transportation Rs.10,000/- has been awarded.
He also submits that claims tribunal for quantifying the compensation for loss of earning capacity has taken the income of the appellant on notional basis at Rs.5500/- per month which is not correct.

The appellant has claimed that he was earning Rs.15000/- per month, however,
the claims tribunal did not accept the same.

He further submits that even if the claim of Rs.15000/-
per month is not believed still he should have been treated as skilled NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35780 3 MA-5449-2022 labourer considering the fact that he was driver.
He thus prays for enhancement of compensation.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the claims tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the appellant inasmuch as he has not examined his employer to establish that he was working as driver and earning Rs.15000/- per month.

He points out that even the driving licence was not exhibited by the claimant/appellant before the claims tribunal and in absence of driving licence and the employer, even the fact that he was working as driver before the accident was not proved by him.
As such, the claims tribunal has not erred in treating him an unskilled labour.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
10.
From perusal of the record it is clear that there were no evidence to support the claim of the appellant that he was working as a driver.

Although, Ex.P-10 salary certified was placed on record,
however, the same was on a plain paper without there being any witness to prove the same.

Similarly, the permanent disability as has been taken by the claims tribunal at 15% is based on the statement of expert witness Dr. Ashish Mehrotra, who himself has stated in para 6 of his cross examination that the fracture has properly got united and there is no mall- union.

He also submitted that after union of fracture, the appellant can bear the weight on his right leg and opined that over all permanent disability can be taken at 15%, in such circumstances, the claims tribunal has taken permanent disability at 15%.

2 11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering these two aspects i.e. the employment of the appellant was not proved and his own expert witness has opined that he suffered over all permanent NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35780 4 MA-5449-2022 disability at 15%,
this Court is not inclined to interfere with the conclusion drawn by the claims tribunal in this behalf.

However, the income of the appellant has not been taken correctly, as even if he is to be considered as unskilled labourer, at the relevant time the minimum wages for an unskilled labourer were Rs.6850/- per month, which is taken as the income of the appellant.
Consequently, the compensation for loss of earning capacity has to be reassessed.

However, considering the fact that meager amount of Rs.10,000/- has been awarded for special diet, attendant and transportation and only Rs.15,000/- has been awarded for pain and suffering and loss of amenities of life.
Instead of quantifying the compensation in different heads, a lump-sum amount of Rs.1,25,000/- is hereby awarded to the appellant over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of application before the claims tribunal.
12. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
